title: Confused Deputy
security_question: May a deputy agent use its own ambient authority for a caller's request, or does CTRL-DELEGATION-001 require that the caller delegated that authority for this operation?
retest_support_detail: ATTACK and RETEST send the same request (lookup_customer_tier, customer:read, cust-001). The caller (Credit Agent) and the deputy (Compliance Agent) are coded server-side; the profile is server-owned ExperimentContext.

BASELINE.attack_objective: Run the delegated request (lookup_policy at policy:read for lending-basics) so the later ATTACK has a normal comparison.
BASELINE.why_this_matters: You need the shape of a legitimate delegation before judging the deputy's extra request.
BASELINE.what_will_change: A new run.id. CTRL-DELEGATION-001 ALLOW delegation_granted; the policy handler runs once, the customer-tier handler does not.
BASELINE.what_will_not_change: The delegated tool set. The browser does not choose the caller, the deputy, the tool or the profile.
BASELINE.security_property: A delegated request, for comparison only.
BASELINE.expected_evidence_defended: testbed.mode=BASELINE, profile=defended, authority source delegated, ALLOW delegation_granted, policy handler 1, customer-tier handler 0.
BASELINE.predict_before_launch: Before you click Launch, write: should this request be allowed, and which handler should run?

ATTACK.attack_objective: Send the deputy a request for lookup_customer_tier, which the caller never delegated, on the intentionally vulnerable ATTACK experiment and observe whose authority it runs under.
ATTACK.why_this_matters: A deputy may possess authority the caller was never allowed to use. AUTHORITY POSSESSED != AUTHORITY DELEGATED.
ATTACK.what_will_change: A new run.id is minted. CTRL-DELEGATION-001 records a labelled fail-open ALLOW and the customer-tier handler runs under the deputy's ambient authority.
ATTACK.what_will_not_change: The delegated tool set and the coded identities. Splunk does not ALLOW or DENY.
ATTACK.security_property: AUTHORITY POSSESSED != AUTHORITY DELEGATED. On this labelled vulnerable profile the lab is fail-open; that is not a universal bypass.
ATTACK.expected_evidence_vulnerable: INTENTIONALLY VULNERABLE LAB PROFILE: ALLOW vulnerable_profile_fail_open:ambient_deputy_authority with authority source ambient_deputy and customer-tier handler 1. ALLOW is not execution by itself; the handler count is.
ATTACK.expected_evidence_defended: Not this ATTACK specimen. The defended outcome is the RETEST experiment.
ATTACK.predict_before_launch: Before you click Launch ATTACK, write: whose authority will the request run under, and will the customer-tier handler start?
ATTACK.attacker_influence: The request the caller makes of the deputy; the attacker wants the deputy's own authority used for it.
ATTACK.defense_should: On this ATTACK specimen the lab is fail-open. The defense you will enable is the RETEST ExperimentContext (profile=defended), not Splunk.

RETEST.attack_objective: Replay the SAME request on the defended RETEST experiment and prove the outcome changed because defense changed, not because the request changed.
RETEST.why_this_matters: A closed-loop experiment needs independent ATTACK and RETEST run.ids.
RETEST.what_will_change: A new run.id, testbed.mode=RETEST, profile=defended; DENY delegated_authority_not_granted, customer-tier handler 0.
RETEST.what_will_not_change: The tool, scope, arguments and request fingerprint. Splunk still does not enforce.
RETEST.security_property: Same request plus different server-owned configuration gives a different outcome. Not universal resistance.
RETEST.which_control: CTRL-DELEGATION-001, before the tool handler. AcmeBank owns enforcement; Splunk does not.
RETEST.falsify: A customer-tier handler start after the DENY, or ALLOW on this RETEST experiment, would falsify the defended prediction. Missing Splunk rows alone would not.
RETEST.predict_before_launch: Will the same request reach the handler? If denied, what evidence should exist?

limitations: LOCAL EDUCATIONAL SERVICE when installed locally. On a remote deployment the learner uses the host in the browser address bar. The service is unauthenticated.
NOT PRODUCTION AUTHENTICATION. NOT MULTI-TENANT. NOT INTERNET-FACING.
CTRL-MCP-001 is a lab allow-list, not production MCP IAM.
JSON-RPC is in-process, not stdio/HTTP MCP transport.
RETEST DENY is not automatically SAFE.
HEC HTTP 200 is not searchable evidence.
Missing mcp.started is not independent proof of prevention.
ALLOW is not execution. DENY is not an incident.
DET-MCP-001 alerts only on DENY-then-start. ATTACK fail-open ALLOW is silent. Silence is not SAFE.
Studio tokens are not auto-bound to a fresh run.id.
Learning metadata is not security policy.
The caller and deputy are coded fixtures, not authenticated agents; there is no A2A transport.
